Things 11–20: Data Quality, Privacy, and Collaboration

第 2 章（共 10 章）：数据质量、隐私与协作（第 11–20 篇）

11. Caution: Data Science Projects Can Turn into the Emperor's New Clothes当心：数据科学项目可能变成皇帝的新衣

Shweta Katre

什维塔·卡特雷

The fourth industrial revolution has dawned: the Age of Analytics. There is a mad rush to develop predictive models and algorithms to establish supremacy in an immensely competitive, data-driven world. Starting off with predictive analytics and moving into the realm of machine learning and artificial intelligence, most companies are expanding their capabilities to spawn data science projects.

第四次工业革命已经到来：分析时代。在这个竞争异常激烈、数据驱动的世界里，大家疯狂地开发预测模型和算法，以求占据优势。从预测分析起步，再迈入机器学习和人工智能的疆域，大多数公司都在扩张能力、孵化数据科学项目。

Enormous pressure is placed on data science teams, like all other kinds of project teams, to deliver business value that is usable and potentially releasable in a specific time frame. A big challenge for data science teams is to show visible and measurable progress/work done, to keep stakeholder interest alive and the funding steady.

和所有其他项目团队一样，数据科学团队承受着巨大压力：必须在给定时间内交付可用、可发布的业务价值。数据科学团队的一大挑战，就是要展示出可见、可衡量的进展和成果，以维持业务方的兴趣和稳定的资金投入。

However, roughly 80% of project time is spent on data collection/selection, data preparation, and exploratory analysis (see the following figure). Project overheads are huge, but there is no visible output. The promised predictive model or algorithm is not revealed in the early or even middle stages. Sometimes, in the evaluation or validation stage, the possibility arises of scrapping the entire analysis and going back to the drawing board. In such scenarios, resources have been used up, hours have been burned, but no output has resulted—à la the emperor's new clothes!

然而，大约 80% 的项目时间都花在数据收集/筛选、数据准备和探索性分析上（见下图）。项目开销巨大，却没有可见产出。承诺的预测模型或算法在早期甚至中期都看不到踪影。有时到了评估或验证阶段，还有可能整个分析被推倒重来。在这种情况下，资源耗尽、时间烧光，却没有产出——活脱脱一出皇帝的新衣！

How do you save your data science team from the emperor embarrassment? Data science projects call for strategic planning and management of priorities, resources, and infrastructure, as outlined in these steps:

你要怎么把数据科学团队从这种“皇帝式尴尬”中拯救出来？数据科学项目需要战略性规划，以及对优先级、资源和基础设施的管理，具体步骤如下：

— p.39 —
  1. Understand the sell-first approach. What basic need were the stakeholders promised your project would meet? The IT industry is moving away from full big-bang deployments. It's all about iterations. No matter how many data sources we scour, or which cutting-edge technology we showcase, data science release road maps should be designed in such a way that every iteration pushes the fulfillment of that very basic need in some direction.
    理解“先卖再做”的思路。业务方当初被承诺你的项目会满足什么基本需求？IT 行业正在告别那种一次性大爆炸式的部署，一切都围绕迭代展开。无论我们搜罗了多少数据源、展示了多么尖端的技术，数据科学的发布路线图都应该这样设计：每一次迭代都朝满足那个基本需求的方向推进一步。
  2. Give a "face" to the project. Not only for the stakeholders but also from a project manager or product owner's perspective, there needs to be a window into what's going on. A user interface (UI) that acts as a face for under-the-hood analytics can help visualize the analytics process and give insight into the project's progress. This UI or dashboard should be interactive and identify the specific datasets being utilized and the exact model used to obtain a specific result set. It can also be used for validation and acceptance among the user group.
    给项目一张“脸”。无论是对业务方，还是从项目经理或产品负责人的角度，都需要有一扇窗让人看到里面在发生什么。一个作为底层分析“脸面”的用户界面（UI），可以把分析过程可视化，并让人洞察项目进展。这个 UI 或仪表盘应当是可交互的，能标明正在使用哪些数据集、用哪个确切模型得到某个结果集。它还可以用于用户群中的验证和验收。
  3. Ensure environment readiness. The development environment should be capable of quickly populating databases and changing datasets for exploratory analysis. Memory management issues are major blockers to most data science projects. Huge amounts of data will be downloaded from various data sources. They could be shapefiles, spreadsheets, or text files. An effective memory management plan for all computing and storage devices in the development environment should be in place.
    确保环境就绪。开发环境应当能够快速填充数据库、切换数据集以做探索性分析。内存管理问题是大多数数据科学项目的主要拦路虎。我们要从各种数据源下载海量数据，可能是 shapefile、电子表格或文本文件。开发环境中所有计算和存储设备都应当有一套有效的内存管理方案。
  4. Catalog scripts. Scripts for downloading data, scripts for data cleansing and preparation, and scripts for data archiving should be tagged appropriately for reuse.
    把脚本编目管理。下载数据的脚本、数据清洗和准备的脚本、数据归档的脚本，都应当打上合适的标签以便复用。
— p.40 —

The data science ecosystem can consist of a diverse data science team, diverse tool sets, and a variety of data. It's the end goal of the project that ties all the analytics effort together. It could result in the formulation of a clever algorithm for AI, or it could result in a failure. Either way, the outcome of steps 1 through 4 will ensure that our stakeholders do not lose faith in our efforts and we do not produce a high-tech version of the emperor's new clothes!

数据科学生态可以由多元化的团队、多元化的工具集和多样化的数据构成。是项目的最终目标把所有分析努力绑在一起。它可能催生一个聪明的 AI 算法，也可能以失败告终。无论哪种结果，上面第 1 到第 4 步的产出都会确保业务方不会对我们的努力失去信心，我们也不会造出一个高科技版的皇帝新衣！

— p.41 —

12. Change Data Capture变更数据捕获（CDC）

Raghotham Murthy

拉戈塔姆·穆尔蒂

Change data capture (CDC) is a solution to a specific problem. You have your most valuable data in your production databases. You want to analyze that data, but you don't want to add any more load to those production databases. Instead, you want to rely on a data warehouse or data lake. Once you decide that you want to analyze data from your production database in a different system, you need a reliable way to replicate that data from the production database to your data warehouse.

变更数据捕获（CDC）是针对一个特定问题的解决方案。你最有价值的数据存在生产数据库里。你想分析这些数据，但不想给生产数据库再加任何负载。你希望转而依赖数据仓库或数据湖。一旦你决定要在另一个系统里分析生产数据库中的数据，就需要一种可靠的方式，把数据从生产库复制到数据仓库。

It turns out, at scale, this is a hard problem to solve. You can't just decide to copy data over from the production database to the warehouse—that would add a lot more load on the production database, especially if you want high fidelity. And if you fetched only the changed records, you would miss deletes. Thankfully, all modern production databases write out a write-ahead log (WAL), or change log, as part of their normal transaction processing. This log captures every single change to each row/cell in each table in the database and can be used in database replication to create replicas of the production database. In CDC, a tool reads this write-ahead log and applies the changes to the data warehouse. This technique is a lot more robust than batch exports of the tables and has a low footprint on the production database.

事实证明，在大规模下这是个难题。你不能简单地决定把数据从生产库拷贝到仓库——那会给生产库增加大量负载，尤其是在你要求高保真的情况下。而如果你只拉取发生变化的记录，又会漏掉删除操作。幸好，所有现代生产数据库在正常事务处理中都会写一个预写日志（WAL），或称变更日志。这个日志捕获数据库中每张表、每一行/每个单元格的每一次变更，可以用于数据库复制来生成生产库的副本。在 CDC 中，一个工具读取这个预写日志，并把变更应用到数据仓库。这种技术比批量导出表要稳健得多，并且对生产库的占用很小。

However, you have to treat CDC as an end-to-end data pipeline in order to correctly replicate data initially as well as on an ongoing basis. You need to consider several aspects of the CDC connector life cycle. Here are a few examples:

然而，你必须把 CDC 当作一条端到端数据管道来对待，才能既在初始阶段、又在持续运行中正确复制数据。你需要考虑 CDC 连接器生命周期的几个方面。下面举几个例子：

Scale规模

The CDC pipeline has to be robust enough for high data volume. For example, in PostgreSQL, delays in reading the WAL can cause the database's disk space to run out!

CDC 管道必须足够稳健，能扛住大数据量。例如在 PostgreSQL 中，读取 WAL 的延迟可能导致数据库磁盘空间被占满！

Replication lag复制延迟

This refers to the duration between the time that a transaction is committed in the primary database and the time it becomes available in the data warehouse. You have to build checks to make sure that your pipeline is minimizing lag time before transformations are run.

它指的是事务在主库提交的时刻，与它在数据仓库中可被查询的时刻之间的时长。你必须建立检查机制，确保在运行转换之前，管道的延迟被压到最小。

— p.42 —

Schema changesSchema 变更

Over time, database schemas evolve because tables or columns are added or removed or types are updated. It is important to propagate the schema changes to the data warehouse. Sometimes a schema change might require a historical sync.

随着时间推移，数据库 schema 会演进，因为表或列被增删、类型被更新。把 schema 变更同步到数据仓库非常重要。有时一次 schema 变更可能需要做一次历史数据同步。

Masking脱敏

You have to mask sensitive columns for compliance purposes.

出于合规目的，你必须对敏感列做脱敏。

Historical syncs历史同步

Before applying the CDC changes, an initial historical sync of the tables is needed. It can take a while and can overload the source. It's better to do historical syncs from a replica database to speed them up and reduce load on the primary database. Sometimes partial interruptions might occur in the WAL, so you need partial historical syncs instead of full historical syncs to recover fast.

在应用 CDC 变更之前，需要先对表做一次初始的历史同步。这可能耗时较长，并压垮源端。更好的做法是从副本数据库做历史同步，以加快速度并减轻主库负载。有时 WAL 可能出现部分中断，这时你需要做部分历史同步而不是全量历史同步，以便快速恢复。

There are typically no strong reasons to build your own CDC connectors. Use existing tools instead!

通常情况下，没有充分理由自己造 CDC 连接器。直接用现成工具吧！

— p.43 —

13. Column Names as Contracts把列名当作契约

Emily Riederer

艾米丽·里德勒

Software products use unit tests and service-level agreements (SLAs) to make performance promises; interfaces have common symbols and labels. However, data tables exist somewhere in between—neither engineered like a service nor designed like an application. This lack of conversation and contract-making between producers and consumers leaves engineers confused about why users aren't satisfied (or make vague complaints of "data quality") and consumers befuddled that the data is never quite "right."

软件产品用单元测试和服务等级协议（SLA）来做性能承诺；接口有统一的符号和标签。然而数据表却处在中间地带——既不像服务那样被工程化，也不像应用那样被设计。生产方与消费方之间缺乏对话和契约订立，结果工程师们搞不懂用户为什么不满意（或者只是模糊地抱怨“数据质量差”），消费方则困惑数据怎么就总是不太“对”。

Using a controlled vocabulary for naming fields in published datasets is a low-tech, low-friction solution to this dilemma. Developing a common language forms a shared understanding of how each field in a dataset is intended to work, and it can also alleviate producer overhead in data validation, documentation, and wrangling.

在对外发布的数据集中，用一套受控词表来命名字段，是解决这个困境的低技术、低摩擦方案。发展出一套共同语言，能让大家对数据集中每个字段的用途形成共识，还能减轻生产方在数据校验、文档和整理上的负担。

Engineers and analysts can define up front a tiered set of stubs with atomic, well-defined meanings. When pieced together, these stubs can be used to describe complex metrics and behaviors.

工程师和分析师可以预先定义一套分层的“词干”，每个词干都有原子化、定义良好的含义。把这些词干拼起来，就可以用来描述复杂的指标和行为。

Imagine you work at a ride-share company and are building a data table with one record per trip. What might a controlled vocabulary look like? A first level might characterize different measures, consisting of both a data type (e.g., bool or int) and appropriate usage patterns. For example:

设想你在一家网约车公司工作，正在构建一张“每次行程一条记录”的表。受控词表会长什么样？第一层可以描述不同的度量，既包含数据类型（例如 bool 或 int），也包含合适的使用模式。例如：

  • ID: Integer. Non-null. Unique identifier for an entity. Likely a primary key.
    ID：整数。非空。某个实体的唯一标识符。通常是主键。
  • IND: Binary. Non-null. Indicator of an event occurrence.
    IND：二进制。非空。表示某事件是否发生的指示符。
  • N: Integer. Non-null. Non-negative count of quantity of event occurrences.
    N：整数。非空。事件发生次数的非负计数。
— p.44 —
  • AMT: Numeric. Summable, continuous "denominator-free" amount.
    AMT：数值型。可求和的连续“无分母”金额。
  • VAL: Numeric. Not inherently summable (e.g., a rate, ratio, latitude, or longitude).
    VAL：数值型。本质上不可求和（例如比率、比例、纬度或经度）。
  • DT: Date. Always in YYYY-MM-DD form.
    DT：日期。永远采用 YYYY-MM-DD 形式。
  • TM: Timestamp.
    TM：时间戳。

The second level might characterize the subject of the measure, such as a DRIVER, RIDER, TRIP, ORIG, or DEST. Additional levels would provide additional "adjectives" to modify the measure subjects. For example, we might have CITY, ZIP, LAT, and LON.

第二层可以描述度量的主体，例如 DRIVER（司机）、RIDER（乘客）、TRIP（行程）、ORIG（起点）或 DEST（终点）。再往下的层级提供更多“形容词”来修饰这些度量主体。例如我们可以有 CITY、ZIP、LAT、LON。

Altogether, this structure provides a grammar to concisely characterize a wide range of metrics. Isn't it fairly self-evident what ID_DRIVER, TM_ORIG, VAL_DEST_LON, and IND_TRIP_SURGE mean?

整套结构合起来，就提供了一套语法，可以简洁地刻画五花八门的指标。ID_DRIVER、TM_ORIG、VAL_DEST_LON、IND_TRIP_SURGE 这些名字的意思，不是不言自明吗？

Not only do these names provide a nice interface for users, but they disambiguate data requirements in important ways that can help directly automate data management tasks. Metadata management and data discoverability tasks can be partially automated by reconstructing variable definitions from stubs (e.g., "unique identifier of a ride-share driver") and allowing users to easily search all tables for a given set of concepts (all timestamps, everything to do with a trip's origin). Similarly, performance contracts promised to users in the top-level stubs can translate seamlessly to automated data-validation checks ("everything that starts with DT should be cast as a date," "nothing in AMT fields should be a decimal," "IND variables must not be null") in tools like Great Expectations. Finally, such variables may prove useful mental guides in your own further munging (e.g., "it doesn't make sense to sum up VAL variables").

这些名字不仅给用户提供了一个友好的接口，还以重要的方式消除了数据需求的歧义，可以直接帮助自动化数据管理任务。元数据管理和数据可发现性任务，可以通过从词干重构变量定义（例如“网约车司机的唯一标识符”）来部分自动化，并允许用户轻松地在所有表中搜索一组概念（所有时间戳、与行程起点相关的一切）。类似地，在顶层词干中向用户承诺的性能契约，可以无缝地转成自动化数据校验规则（“所有以 DT 开头的字段都应转成日期”“AMT 字段里不应出现小数”“IND 变量不得为空”），在 Great Expectations 这类工具中落地。最后，这类变量名在你自己后续的数据整理中也可以充当有用的思维指南（例如“把 VAL 变量加总毫无意义”）。

Of course, no single, silver-bullet solution exists for data quality, discoverability, and communication. But using column names to form contracts is a useful way to start communicating both with your users and your workflow tools.

当然，数据质量、可发现性和沟通问题没有什么银弹。但用列名来形成契约，是开始与用户、与工作流工具对话的一个有效起点。

— p.45 —

14. Consensual, Privacy-Aware Data Collection经同意、有隐私意识的数据采集

Katharine Jarmul

凯瑟琳·贾穆尔

How consensual is your data collection? Are customers aware of how their data is being used? Do they know how it is transformed, aggregated, fed into a model, and deployed? Is it being done with respect for their privacy? Can they ask for it not to be included in any of those automated processes? Do you have privacy-protection mechanisms to ensure that sensitive data is not at risk?

你的数据采集有多大程度是“经同意”的？客户知道他们的数据是怎么被使用的吗？他们知道数据是如何被转换、聚合、喂入模型并部署的吗？这一切是否在尊重他们隐私的前提下进行？他们能否要求把自己的数据从这些自动化流程中排除？你有没有隐私保护机制，确保敏感数据不会处于风险之中？

As data engineers, we aim for precision and efficiency. How can we get data from place A to place B, with the necessary in-between steps for cleaning, testing, and validation, and how can we do that most efficiently?

作为数据工程师，我们追求精准和高效。怎样把数据从 A 地搬到 B 地，并在中间做必要的清洗、测试和校验？怎样做得最有效率？

What gets lost in this objective to expedite and automate processing is that we are often handling personal data—sometimes extremely sensitive data. And if you've had the pleasure of working with European Union (EU) residents' data, you might have thought about these topics further because of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). How can we remove artifacts from users whose data we no longer have rights to? What does it mean for a person to be subject to automated processing? What does consensual data collection look like?

在这种“加速和自动化处理”的目标中，被我们忽略的是：我们常常在处理个人数据——有时是极度敏感的数据。如果你曾经有幸处理过欧盟（EU）居民的数据，你可能因为《通用数据保护条例》（GDPR）而对这些话题想得更深。我们怎样把那些我们不再有权持有的用户数据从系统产物中删掉？一个人“受自动化处理约束”意味着什么？经同意的数据采集应该长什么样？

If we want to collect data consensually—for all people, not just those lucky enough to reside in the EU—we need to fundamentally change some of the ways we move data. Here are some ideas on how we can get started.

如果我们想为所有人（而不仅仅是那些有幸居住在欧盟的人）做经同意的数据采集，就需要从根本上改变我们搬数据的一些方式。下面是一些可以起步的想法。

Attach Consent Metadata附上同意元数据

We can do this as part of our processing. We have the means to determine who this user is and what they consented to or opted out of. We can filter or reroute their data depending on their level of consent. This means we can also implement better user experiences for those who want to opt out of some processing (i.e., slightly less awful cookie alerts!).

我们可以在处理流程中做到这一点。我们有办法识别这个用户是谁、他们同意了什么、退出了什么。我们可以根据他们的同意级别过滤或改道他们的数据。这也意味着，我们可以为那些希望退出某些处理的人提供更好的用户体验（比如，不那么糟糕的 cookie 提示！）。

— p.46 —

Track Data Provenance追踪数据来源

Do you know where all your data came from? Unfortunately, for many of us, the answer is no. Tracking data provenance not only allows for better understanding of legal and privacy-related concerns, but also helps us determine data quality and what processing might have been applied to the data before it got to us. It's a win-win!

你知道自己所有的数据都是从哪儿来的吗？不幸的是，对我们很多人来说答案是否定的。追踪数据来源不仅能让我们更好地理解法律和隐私相关的问题，还能帮我们判断数据质量，以及数据在到达我们之前经历过什么处理。这是双赢！

Drop or Encrypt Sensitive Fields丢弃或加密敏感字段

We should apply data-protection mechanisms when we know the sensitive fields our data may contain. Do we really need usernames for aggregate analytics? Nope? Then drop them (or don't collect them in the first place). Do we need email addresses for our chatbot training? Nope? Then make sure they don't make it into the model. As data engineers, we can apply our knowledge and tools to ensure that sensitive data is protected.

当我们知道数据里可能含有哪些敏感字段时，就应当施加数据保护机制。聚合分析真的需要用户名吗？不需要？那就丢掉（或者从一开始就别收集）。训练聊天机器人真的需要邮箱地址吗？不需要？那就确保它们进不了模型。作为数据工程师，我们可以运用自己的知识和工具，确保敏感数据受到保护。

Many of us take a variety of measures to protect the privacy of ourselves and our loved ones. Extend the courtesy to the customers and users of the products you create by implementing consensual data collection and basic data-privacy measures.

我们很多人会采取各种措施保护自己和家人的隐私。把这份周到延伸到你所创造产品的客户和用户身上吧——去落实经同意的数据采集和基本的数据隐私措施。

— p.47 —

15. Cultivate Good Working Relationships with Data Consumers培养与数据消费方的良好协作关系

Ido Shlomo

伊多·什洛莫

The relationship between data engineers and data consumers—whether they're data scientists, business intelligence (BI) teams, or one of a multitude of analytics teams—is always complex. All of these functions exist to serve the overall data-driven goals of the organization and are expected to integrate seamlessly. So there is clear motivation to cooperate, but more often than not, the division of labor is far from balanced—a situation that can develop into real tension between the teams.

数据工程师与数据消费方——无论他们是数据科学家、商业智能（BI）团队，还是众多分析团队中的一支——之间的关系总是复杂的。所有这些职能都是为了服务组织整体的数据驱动目标而存在，也被期望能够无缝整合。因此合作的动机是明确的，但分工往往远谈不上平衡——这种状况可能演变为团队之间真正的紧张关系。

There is no recipe for creating a perfect symbiotic relationship, and this is doubly true given the great amount of variation in the structure of data teams across organizations. That said, the following points can help data engineers avoid major pitfalls and aim for a better direction.

没有什么配方能造出完美的共生关系，考虑到不同组织中数据团队结构千差万别，这一点尤其成立。尽管如此，下面几点可以帮助数据工程师避开大坑，朝更好的方向努力。

Don't Let Consumers Solve Engineering Problems别让消费方去解决工程问题

Avoid the temptation of letting data consumers solve data-engineering problems. Many types of data consumers exist, and the core competencies of each individual vary across multiple spectrums—coding skills, statistical knowledge, visualization abilities, and more. In many cases, the more technically capable data consumers will attempt to close infrastructure gaps themselves by applying ad hoc fixes. This can take the form of applying additional data transformations to a pipeline that isn't serving its purpose or even actual infrastructure design.

要克制住“让数据消费方去解决数据工程问题”的诱惑。数据消费方有很多种，每个人的核心能力在多个维度上参差不齐——编码能力、统计知识、可视化能力等等。很多时候，技术能力更强的消费方会自己动手，用临时补丁来填补基础设施的缺口。这可能表现为：在一条已经不堪用的管道上再叠加数据转换，甚至是直接做基础设施设计。

Superficially, it may appear to the data engineer as a win-win situation: their own time is saved, and the consumer's work proceeds unhindered. However, this usually results in convoluted layers of suboptimal solutions that make the organization's data infrastructure increasingly hard to manage.

表面上看，对数据工程师似乎是双赢：自己的时间省下来了，消费方的工作也没被耽误。然而，这通常会导致一层层绕来绕去的次优方案，让组织的数据基础设施越来越难管。

— p.48 —

Adapt Your Expectations调整你的期望

Avoid applying engineering sensibilities to data consumers. As fully trained developers, data engineers usually follow contemporary programming best practices. These imply stringent coding style and focus on efficiency and unit-test coverage. Some organizations opt for very close-knit data teams or even unify all of the functions inside a single DataOps team.

不要把工程师的那套敏感性套在数据消费方身上。作为训练有素的开发者，数据工程师通常遵循当代编程最佳实践，包括严格的代码风格、对效率和单元测试覆盖率的关注。有些组织选择关系非常紧密的数据团队，甚至把所有职能统一到一个 DataOps 团队里。

In such cases, data engineers should tailor their expectations to those of data consumers who work intensively with code but do not follow those best practices. This is usually not motivated by ignorance on their part, but is rather adherence to their primary business function, which requires that they prioritize other things.

在这种情况下，数据工程师应当把期望调整到与数据消费方匹配——他们虽然大量和代码打交道，却不遵循那些最佳实践。这通常不是因为他们无知，而是因为他们要服务于自己的主要业务职能，必须把别的事情放在优先位置。

Understand Consumers' Jobs理解消费方的工作

Put a premium on knowing what data consumers actually do. Data consumers rely on data infrastructure to do their respective jobs. Their level of comfort, productivity, and adoption depends on the fit between that infrastructure and the dynamics of their work. Data engineers are tasked with developing this infrastructure from conception to implementation, and the actual day-to-day needs of the respective consumers are therefore critical context.

把“搞清楚数据消费方实际在做什么”放在重要位置。数据消费方依靠数据基础设施来完成各自的工作。他们的顺手程度、生产力和采纳程度，取决于这套基础设施与他们工作节奏之间的匹配度。数据工程师负责从构想到落地地建设这套基础设施，因此消费方日常的真实需求就是至关重要的上下文。

This usually implies spending both time and effort to get a clear read, whether in the form of shadowing sessions, iterative proofs of concept (POCs), or both low- and high-level ideation discussions. The increase in professional familiarity between the teams also leads to an increase in mutual respect and amiability, and that in itself is a powerful driver of success.

这通常意味着要花时间和精力去清晰理解，无论是通过跟班观察、迭代式概念验证（POC），还是通过从细节到宏观的各种构想讨论。团队之间专业熟悉度的提升，也会带来相互尊重和融洽关系的提升，而这本身就是成功的强大驱动力。

— p.49 —

16. Data Engineering != Spark数据工程 ≠ Spark

Jesse Anderson

杰西·安德森

The misconception that Apache Spark is all you'll need for your data pipeline is common. The reality is that you're going to need components from three general types of technologies to create a data pipeline. These three general types of big data technologies are: Computation, Storage, Messaging.

“做数据管道只需要 Apache Spark 就够了”这种误解很常见。实际情况是：要搭一条数据管道，你需要从三大类技术中选取组件。这三大类大数据技术是：计算、存储、消息。

Fixing and remedying this misconception is crucial to success with big data projects or one's own learning about big data. Spark is just one part of a larger big data ecosystem that's necessary to create data pipelines. Put another way:

纠正这个误解，对大数据项目的成功、对个人学习大数据都至关重要。Spark 只是更大的大数据生态中的一部分，而要搭建数据管道，整个生态都是需要的。换句话说：

Data Engineering = Computation + Storage + Messaging + Coding + Architecture + Domain Knowledge + Use Cases

数据工程 = 计算 + 存储 + 消息 + 编码 + 架构 + 领域知识 + 用例

Batch and Real-Time Systems批处理与实时系统

Generally, you have to solve two core problems in a batch data pipeline. The first is computation, and the second is the storage of data. Spark is a good solution for handling batch computation, but it can be more difficult to find the right storage solution—or more correctly, to identify the different and optimized storage technologies for your use case.

一般来说，在批处理数据管道中你要解决两个核心问题：第一是计算，第二是数据存储。Spark 是处理批计算的好方案，但要找到合适的存储方案——或者更准确地说，为你的用例找出不同的、经过优化的存储技术——可能要难得多。

Computation Component计算组件

Computation is how your data gets processed. Computation frameworks are responsible for running the algorithms and the majority of your code. For big data, they're responsible for resource allocation, running the code in a distributed fashion, and persisting the results.

计算就是数据被处理的方式。计算框架负责运行算法和你的大部分代码。对于大数据，它们还要负责资源分配、以分布式方式运行代码、以及把结果持久化。

— p.50 —

Storage Component存储组件

Storage is how your data gets persisted permanently. For simple storage requirements, people will just dump their files into a directory. As the requirements become slightly more difficult, we start to use partitioning. This will put files in directories with specific names. A common partitioning method is to use the date of the data as part of the directory name.

存储就是数据被永久保存的方式。对于简单的存储需求，人们直接把文件丢进一个目录。当需求稍微复杂一点，我们就开始用分区。这会把文件放进具有特定命名的目录中。一种常见的分区方式是把数据日期作为目录名的一部分。

NoSQL DatabasesNoSQL 数据库

For more optimized storage requirements, we start using NoSQL databases. The need for NoSQL databases is especially prevalent when you have a real-time system. Most companies store data in both a simple storage technology and one or more NoSQL databases. Storing data multiple times accommodates the different use cases or read/write patterns that are necessary. One application may need to read everything, and another application may need only specific data.

对于更讲究优化的存储需求，我们开始使用 NoSQL 数据库。当你有实时系统时，对 NoSQL 数据库的需求尤其普遍。大多数公司既用简单存储技术，也用一个或多个 NoSQL 数据库来存数据。多份存储是为了适配不同的用例或读写模式。一个应用可能需要读全部数据，另一个应用可能只需要特定数据。

Messaging Component消息组件

Messaging is how knowledge or events get passed in real time. You start to use messaging when there is a need for real-time systems. These messaging frameworks are used to ingest and disseminate a large amount of data. This ingestion and dissemination is crucial to real-time systems because it solves the first-mile and last-mile problems.

消息就是知识或事件被实时传递的方式。当需要实时系统时，你就开始用消息。这些消息框架用于接入和传播大量数据。这种接入和传播对实时系统至关重要，因为它解决了“第一英里”和“最后一英里”问题。

1 A version of this chapter was originally published at jesse-anderson.com.

注 1：本章的一个版本最初发表于 jesse-anderson.com。

— p.51 —

17. Data Engineering for Autonomy and Rapid Innovation为自主性与快速创新而做数据工程

Jeff Magnusson

杰夫·马格努森

In many organizations, data engineering is treated purely as a specialty. Data pipelines are seen as the complex, arcane domain of data engineers. Often data engineers are organized into dedicated teams, or embedded into vertically oriented product-based teams.

在许多组织里，数据工程被纯粹当作一种专业特长。数据管道被视为数据工程师那个复杂、晦涩的领地。数据工程师常被组织成专门的团队，或者嵌入到面向垂直产品的团队中。

While delegating work to specialists often makes sense, it also implies that a handoff is required in order to accomplish something that spans beyond that specialty. Fortunately, with the right frameworks and infrastructure in place, handoffs are unnecessary to accomplish (and, perhaps more importantly, iterate on!) many data flows and tasks.

把工作委托给专家通常是合理的，但这也意味着：要完成任何超出该专业范围的事情，都需要一次交接。幸运的是，只要有合适的框架和基础设施，在完成（或许更重要的是：迭代！）许多数据流和任务时，就不再需要交接。

Data pipelines can generally be decomposed into business or algorithmic logic (metric computation, model training, featurization, etc.) and data-flow logic (complex joins, data wrangling, sessionization, etc.). Data engineers specialize in implementing data-flow logic, but often must implement other logic to spec based on the desires or needs of the team requesting the work, and without the ability to autonomously adjust those requirements.

数据管道大体上可以拆成业务/算法逻辑（指标计算、模型训练、特征工程等）和数据流逻辑（复杂 join、数据整理、会话化等）。数据工程师专长于实现数据流逻辑，但常常还必须根据提出需求团队的意愿，按规格实现其他逻辑，而且无法自主调整那些需求。

This happens because both types of logic are typically intertwined and implemented hand-in-hand throughout the pipelines. Instead, look for ways to decouple data-flow logic from other forms of logic within the pipeline. Here are some strategies.

之所以这样，是因为这两类逻辑通常交织在一起，在整条管道中并肩实现。相反，要想办法把数据流逻辑与管道中其他形式的逻辑解耦。下面是一些策略。

Implement Reusable Patterns in the ETL Framework在 ETL 框架中实现可复用模式

Rather than turning common patterns into templates, implement them as functions within an ETL framework. This minimizes code skew and maintenance burden, and makes data pipelines more accessible to contributors beyond the data-engineering team.

与其把常见模式做成模板，不如把它们作为函数实现在一个 ETL 框架里。这样能最大限度减少代码偏差和维护负担，并让数据工程团队之外的贡献者也更容易参与数据管道的开发。

— p.52 —

Choose a Framework and Tool Set Accessible Within the Organization选择组织内大家都能上手的框架和工具集

One reason data engineering is viewed as a specialty is that data pipelines are often implemented in a language or tool set that is not common to the rest of the organization. Consider adopting a framework that supports a language that is widely known and used within your organization (hint: SQL is widely known and understood outside the data-engineering specialty).

数据工程之所以被视为一种“专业特长”，一个原因是数据管道常用一种组织里其他人不熟悉的语言或工具集来实现。可以考虑采用一个支持组织内广为人知、被广泛使用的语言的框架（提示：SQL 在数据工程专业之外也广为人知、被广泛理解）。

Move the Logic to the Edges of the Pipelines把逻辑移到管道的边缘

Look to move data-flow logic as far upstream or downstream as possible. This allows the remainder of the work to happen as a pre- or post-processing step, effectively decoupling the data engineers from data consumers, and restoring autonomy to iterate without further handoffs.

想办法把数据流逻辑尽可能往上游或下游推。这样剩下的工作就可以作为预处理或后处理步骤完成，从而有效地把数据工程师和数据消费方解耦，恢复无需进一步交接即可迭代的自主性。

Create and Support Staging Tables创建并支持 Staging 表

Staging tables are often employed as intermediate checkpoints or outputs between jobs in data pipelines. However, they are often treated as ephemeral datasets used only by the pipeline they run in. If you need to implement a tricky or expensive join or processing step, consider staging out the results and supporting their use by other, less specialized folks within the organization.

Staging 表常被用作数据管道中各个作业之间的中间检查点或输出。然而，它们常被视为只在所在管道中使用的临时数据集。如果你需要实现一个棘手或昂贵的 join 或处理步骤，考虑把结果落地为 staging 表，并支持组织里其他不那么专业的人使用。

Bake Data-Flow Logic into Tooling and Infrastructure把数据流逻辑烘焙进工具和基础设施

Bake common patterns into frameworks or tooling that is invoked via configuration. Data-engineering logic can often be highly leveraged by pushing it into data acquisition, access, or storage code. Rather than expressing the configuration of data-flow logic within data pipelines, consider embedding it in the metadata store as metadata on input or output data sources.

把常见模式烘焙进通过配置即可调用的框架或工具中。数据工程逻辑通常可以被高度复用，方法是把它下推到数据采集、访问或存储代码中。与其在数据管道内部表达数据流逻辑的配置，不如把它作为输入/输出数据源上的元数据，嵌入到元数据存储中。

— p.53 —

18. Data Engineering from a Data Scientist's Perspective数据科学家眼中的数据工程

Bill Franks

比尔·弗兰克斯

People have focused on the ingestion and management of data for decades, but only recently has data engineering become a widespread role. Why is that? This chapter offers a somewhat contrarian view.

人们关注数据接入和管理已经几十年了，但数据工程作为一个广泛存在的岗位还是最近的事。为什么会这样？本章提供一个略带反潮流的视角。

Database Administration, ETL, and Such数据库管理、ETL 之类

Historically, people working with enterprise data focused on three primary areas. First were those who manage raw data collection into source systems. Second were those focused on ETL operations. Until recently, ETL roles were overwhelmingly focused on relational databases. Third were database administrators who manage those relational systems.

从历史上看，和企业数据打交道的人主要集中在三个领域。第一类是把原始数据采集进源系统的人。第二类是专注于 ETL 操作的人。直到最近，ETL 岗位绝大多数都围绕关系数据库。第三类是管理这些关系系统的数据库管理员。

The work of these traditional data roles is largely standardized. For example, database administrators don't tell a database which disks to store data on or how to ensure relational integrity. Since relational technology is mature, many complex tasks are easy. Similarly, ETL tools have adapters for common source systems, functionality to handle common transformation operations, and hooks into common destination repositories. For years, a small number of mature tools interfaced with a small number of mature data repositories. Life was relatively simple!

这些传统数据岗位的工作很大程度上已经标准化。例如，数据库管理员不需要告诉数据库把数据存在哪块磁盘上，也不需要操心如何保证关系完整性。由于关系技术已经成熟，许多复杂任务变得容易。类似地，ETL 工具带有常见源系统的适配器、处理常见转换操作的功能，以及接入常见目标仓库的钩子。多年来，就是一小撮成熟工具对接一小撮成熟数据仓库。日子相对简单！

Why the Need for Data Engineers?为什么需要数据工程师？

The roles described previously still exist today in their traditional states. However, those roles are no longer sufficient. Data engineers have stepped in to fill the void.

前面描述的那些岗位，今天仍以传统形态存在。然而，这些岗位已经不够用了。数据工程师走上前来填补了这个空白。

— p.54 —

Today, we have many new data types that aren't friendly to ETL tools or relational databases, and so new tools are needed. However, most of these new tools and repositories are not yet mature and require complex coding. Worse, it is often necessary to integrate multiple immature technologies. Data engineers figure out how to do this integration, often with few documented examples. It takes hard work to get the pieces of a data pipeline to work together efficiently and securely, and it often requires more energy input and complexity than should be needed.

今天，我们有许多新数据类型对 ETL 工具和关系数据库并不友好，因此需要新工具。然而这些新工具和新仓库大多还不成熟，需要复杂的编码。更糟的是，常常需要把多种不成熟的技术集成在一起。数据工程师要搞清楚怎么做这种集成，而有文档的范例往往少得可怜。要让数据管道的各个片段高效、安全地协同工作，需要付出艰苦努力，而且所需的精力和复杂度往往超出应有的水平。

Adding even more complexity are architectures spanning internal systems and external cloud environments. Outsiders say, "Just pull that data together for us; what's the holdup?" But, alas, tasks can be simple to define yet difficult to execute.

更复杂的是那些横跨内部系统和外部云环境的架构。外行会说：“把那些数据给我们拉到一起就行了，卡在哪儿？”可是，唉，任务定义起来简单，执行起来却难。

There are differences between data engineers and traditional data professionals. First, data engineers need to be more skilled at creative problem solving. Next, data engineers need to embrace and use an ever-wider array of tools and approaches. Last, data engineers must focus on integration and optimization across tools and platforms as opposed to optimizing workloads within a given tool or platform.

数据工程师和传统数据专业人士之间是有区别的。第一，数据工程师需要更擅长创造性地解决问题。第二，数据工程师需要拥抱并使用越来越广泛的工具和方法。最后，数据工程师必须专注于跨工具、跨平台的集成与优化，而不是在某个给定工具或平台内部优化工作负载。

What's the Future?未来会怎样？

Much of what data engineers do today via brute force will become standardized over time. This illustrates a parallel between data science and data engineering. A lot of what used to take a data scientist's time is being automated and standardized. "Citizen data scientists" now handle a lot, while data scientists focus on harder problems. We will soon see "citizen data engineers" who make use of standardized data-engineering tools to handle the basics, while data engineers focus on the new frontiers.

今天数据工程师靠蛮力做的很多事情，随着时间推移会被标准化。这与数据科学呈现出一种平行关系。过去要占用数据科学家大量时间的很多工作，正在被自动化和标准化。“公民数据科学家”现在能处理很多事情，数据科学家则专注于更难的问题。我们很快也会看到“公民数据工程师”——他们用标准化的数据工程工具处理基础工作，数据工程师则专注于新的前沿。

1 This chapter is based on a post published on the International Institute for Analytics blog.

注 1：本章基于 International Institute for Analytics 博客上发表的一篇文章。

— p.55 —

19. Data Pipeline Design Patterns for Reusability and Extensibility面向复用与扩展的数据管道设计模式

Mukul Sood

穆库尔·苏德

Designing extensible, modular, reusable data pipelines is a large topic that's relevant in data engineering, as it requires dealing with constant change across different layers such as data sources, ingestion, validation, processing, security, logging, and monitoring. These changes happen at varying rates across the layers and impact data pipelines differently depending on the pipeline's level of abstraction and design.

设计可扩展、模块化、可复用的数据管道，是数据工程中一个很大的话题，因为它要应对跨层的持续变化——数据源、接入、校验、处理、安全、日志、监控等。这些变化在各层以不同速率发生，并根据管道的抽象层次和设计以不同方式影响管道。

To provide context for the layers of a data pipeline and to start to map the configuration, the pipeline can be seen in a distilled form as comprising Ingestion, Processing, and Result layers. For each layer, we can think in terms of functions that map to functional blocks. The content of the blocks changes depending on the layer requirements. This helps us think in terms of templates and configuration that could represent the pipeline's directed acyclic graph (DAG).

为了给数据管道的各层提供上下文，并开始映射配置，可以把管道浓缩地看作由接入层、处理层和结果层组成。对每一层，我们可以用映射到功能块的函数来思考。这些功能块的内容随各层需求而变。这帮助我们从模板和配置的角度思考，用它们来表达管道的有向无环图（DAG）。

The Ingestion, Processing, and Result layers could be mapped to different loggers and monitors based on requirements. For example, in the Ingestion layer, the file log could be S3, the event log could be custom, and the monitors could be Google Cloud operations and Redash. However, the Results layer could be mapped to a DataDog event log and event monitor.

接入层、处理层和结果层可以根据需求映射到不同的日志记录器和监控器。例如，在接入层，文件日志可以是 S3，事件日志可以是自定义的，监控器可以是 Google Cloud operations 和 Redash。而结果层可以映射到 DataDog 事件日志和事件监控器。

If we take a generic pipeline, specifically looking at logging and monitoring, this representation would be implemented as DAG methods, where loggers and monitors would be coupled with DAG code. This involves more coding and is brittle, difficult to reuse, and a violation of design principles including the single-responsibility principle (SRP), Don't Repeat Yourself (DRY), and open/closed—making the overall pipeline unstable and unreliable. If we extend this beyond monitoring and logging, we will see similar problems in different functional blocks—data quality/validation, security/privacy, etc.

如果我们拿一条通用管道，专门看日志和监控，这种表示会被实现为 DAG 的方法，日志记录器和监控器就和 DAG 代码耦合在一起。这需要写更多代码，而且脆弱、难以复用，还违反了设计原则——包括单一职责原则（SRP）、不要重复自己（DRY）和开闭原则——让整条管道不稳定、不可靠。如果把这一点延伸到监控和日志之外，我们会在不同功能块中看到类似问题：数据质量/校验、安全/隐私等。

— p.56 —

When we see similarities in problems, that is an indicator to recognize the common themes. In addition, we want to remove the coupling between implementations and increase cohesion within them. This gives us enough context to start thinking in terms of design patterns (refer to Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software by Erich Gamma et al. [Addison-Wesley]).

当我们看到问题之间的相似性时，那就是一个信号：要识别出共同主题。此外，我们希望去掉实现之间的耦合，提高实现内部的内聚。这给了我们足够的上下文，开始从设计模式的角度思考（参见 Erich Gamma 等人所著《Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software》[Addison-Wesley]）。

The first set of patterns are creational or structural. They allow us to separate creation and structure of cross-cutting concerns such as logging and monitoring from DAG-specific areas. The factory and abstract factory patterns help in abstracting and decoupling the different loggers and monitors from the DAG code, allowing the DAG codebase to evolve without dependencies on the logging and monitoring codebase.

第一组模式是创建型或结构型。它们让我们把日志、监控这类横切关注点的创建与结构，从 DAG 相关代码中分离出来。工厂模式和抽象工厂模式帮助把不同的日志记录器、监控器从 DAG 代码中抽象和解耦出来，让 DAG 代码库可以独立演进，而不依赖日志和监控的代码库。

The second set of patterns are behavioral. They allow us to specify behavior while maintaining DRY and SOLID principles. The decorator pattern is widely used to modify or add behavior to existing functions. Logging and monitoring are immediately applicable.

第二组模式是行为型。它们让我们在保持 DRY 和 SOLID 原则的同时指定行为。装饰器模式被广泛用于修改或给已有函数增加行为。日志和监控是立即可应用的场景。

The facade pattern is useful when a narrower or specific API is needed for the client or consumer. For example, the broad set of APIs or methods exposed by the different loggers and monitors do not need to be exposed to the DAG layer. The facade pattern helps define an access or interface to the logging and monitoring layer.

当客户端或消费方需要一个更窄、更特定的 API 时，外观模式就很有用。例如，不同日志记录器和监控器暴露的那一大套 API 或方法，并不需要暴露给 DAG 层。外观模式帮助定义访问日志和监控层的接口。

When we combine these patterns, we realize the benefits of design principles, as the separation of responsibilities allows the modularization of the codebase at multiple levels: DAG, cross-cutting concerns (separate packages for monitoring and logging), cross-DAG (common templates can be abstracted). This provides building blocks for generalizing the data pipelines to move away from writing custom code to more generic modules, templates, and configuration. The different pieces follow their own development cycles and deployment packages, completely decoupled from the DAG codebase.

当我们把这些模式组合起来，就能体会到设计原则的好处：职责分离让代码库在多个层次上模块化——DAG、横切关注点（监控和日志分成独立包）、跨 DAG（公共模板可被抽象出来）。这为数据管道的通用化提供了积木，让我们从写定制代码转向更通用的模块、模板和配置。各个片段遵循自己的开发周期和部署包，与 DAG 代码库完全解耦。

Adding these design principles does increase the level of abstraction and complexity. However, that is a small price to pay for scaling up the pipeline development while maintaining quality and velocity.

加入这些设计原则确实提高了抽象层次和复杂度。然而，相对于“在保证质量和速度的同时扩大管道开发规模”这一目标，这个代价很小。

— p.57 —

20. Data Quality for Data Engineers数据工程师的数据质量观

Katharine Jarmul

凯瑟琳·贾穆尔

If you manage and deploy data pipelines, how do you ensure they are working? Do you test that data is going through? Do you monitor uptime? Do you even have tests? If so, what exactly do you test?

如果你管理和部署数据管道，你怎么确保它们在正常工作？你有没有测试数据真的在流过？有没有监控正常运行时间？你到底有没有测试？如果有，你测的究竟是什么？

Data pipelines aren't too dissimilar to other pipelines in our world (gas, oil, water). They need to be engineered; they have a defined start and end point. They need to be tested for leaks and regularly monitored. But unlike most data pipelines, these "real-world" pipelines also test the quality of what they carry. Regularly.

数据管道和我们这个世界里的其他管道（煤气、石油、自来水）没太大区别。它们需要被工程化；有明确的起点和终点。需要做泄漏测试并定期监控。但与大多数数据管道不同的是，这些“真实世界”的管道还会定期检测所输送物质的质量。

When was the last time you tested your data pipeline for data quality? When was the last time you validated the schema of the incoming or transformed data, or tested for the appropriate ranges of values (i.e., "common sense" testing)? How do you ensure that low-quality data is either flagged or managed in a meaningful way?

你上一次为数据质量测试自己的数据管道是什么时候？你上一次校验输入或转换后数据的 schema、或者测试数值是否落在合理范围（即“常识性”测试）是什么时候？你怎么确保低质量数据要么被标记出来，要么被有意义地处理？

More than ever before—given the growth and use of large-scale data pipelines—data validation, testing, and quality checks are critical to business needs. It doesn't necessarily matter that we collect 1TB of data a day if that data is essentially useless for tasks like data science, machine learning, or business intelligence because of poor quality control.

鉴于大规模数据管道的增长和使用，数据校验、测试和质量检查对业务需求的重要性前所未有。如果因为质量控制差，每天收集的 1TB 数据对数据科学、机器学习或商业智能等任务基本上毫无用处，那收集多少量并不重要。

We need data engineers to operate like other pipeline engineers—to be concerned about and focused on the quality of what's running through their pipelines. Data engineers should coordinate with the data science team or implement standard testing. This can be as simple as schema validation and null checks. Ideally, you could also test for expected value ranges and private or sensitive data exposure, or sample data over time for statistical testing (i.e., testing distributions or other properties the data at large should have).

我们需要数据工程师像其他管道工程师那样行事——关心并聚焦于流经自己管道的东西的质量。数据工程师应当与数据科学团队协作，或者落地标准测试。这可以简单到只是 schema 校验和空值检查。理想情况下，你还可以测试预期值范围、敏感数据泄露，或者随时间抽样数据做统计检验（即检验数据整体应有的分布或其他属性）。

And the neat thing is, you can use your data knowledge and apply it to these problems. Do you know how many extreme values, anomalies, or outliers your pipeline will expect today? Probably not. But could you? Why, yes, you could. Tracking, monitoring, and inferring the types of errors and quality issues you see in your pipelines or processing is—in and of itself—a meaningful data science task.

妙的是，你可以运用自己的数据知识来解决这些问题。你知道你的管道今天会遇到多少极值、异常或离群点吗？大概不知道。但你能不能知道？当然能。追踪、监控并推断你在管道或处理中看到的错误类型和质量问题，这件事本身就是一项有意义的数据科学任务。

— p.58 —

So please, don't merely see data coming in and going out and say, "Looks good to me." Take the time to determine what quality and validation measurements make sense for your data source and destination, and set up ways to ensure that you can meet those standards. Not only will your data science and business teams thank you for the increase in data quality and utility, but you can also feel proud of your title: engineer.

所以请别只是看着数据流进流出就说“看着没问题”。花点时间，弄清楚对你的数据源和数据目的地来说，什么样的质量和校验指标是有意义的，并建立机制确保你能达到这些标准。这样不仅你的数据科学和业务团队会因为数据质量和可用性的提升而感谢你，你也可以为自己的头衔感到自豪：工程师。

— p.59 —
